correctness.rationale: PASS. Multiplying by x gives yx=N(x)+a. For y≠0, taking norm reduces every preimage uniquely to a nonzero root r in F_q of r²+(Tr(a)-N(y))r+N(a)=0; conversely x=(r+a)/y has norm r and returns exactly y. The zero target is a q+1 norm fiber precisely for a in F_q*. For odd q the discriminant D(z)=(z-Tr(a))²-4N(a), split-character sum -1 and distinguished D(0) classes yield all zero/one/two-root norm counts; for even q absolute trace distinguishes the base/outside cases and double root z=Tr(a). Multiplying each nonzero norm class by q+1 targets and counting coefficients reproduces all table entries. An independent finite-field enumeration of every nonzero a and every nonzero x for q=2,3,5,7,11 confirmed all 5 cases, class sizes and image/fiber histograms (17,353 evaluated (a,x) pairs). The algebra proves all prime powers, not this finite experiment.
